{{nihongo|'''Keta Shrine'''|気多神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Fushiki Ichinomiya, {{ill|Takaoka, Toyama|Q502988|qid=Q502988}}, {{ill|Toyama Prefecture|Q132929|qid=Q132929}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} or minor shrine) and an {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Etchū Province|ckb|پارێزگای ئێتچو|cs|Provincie Eččú|de|Provinz Etchū|es|Provincia de Etchū|fa|ولایت اتچو|fr|Province d'Etchū|gl|Provincia de Etchū|id|Provinsi Etchū|it|Etchū|ja|越中国|ko|엣추국|lt|Ečiū žemė|nl|Etchu (provincie)|pt|Província de Etchū|ru|Эттю (провинция)|simple|Etchū Province|sk|Eččú (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечу|tr|Etchū (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Еттю|vi|Tỉnh Etchū|zh|越中國|zh_min_nan|Ettyû-kok|zh_yue|越中國|qid=Q906899}}. Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was designated a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. {{nihongo|'''Keta Shrine'''|気多神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Etchū Province]].

Fushiki in Takaoka City, where the shrine is located, was once the central area of Etchū Province where the {{ill|Kokufu|Q1629088|qid=Q1629088}} and {{ill|Provincial temple|Q1207757|qid=Q1207757}} existed, and within the shrine grounds there is a traditional site said to be the former location of the {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}}. Among the four shrines within Etchū Province that claim the title of Ichinomiya, this is the only one whose place name includes the appellation “Ichinomiya.”

== History ==
== Founding ==
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was established by the {{ill|Bunrei|Q195793|qid=Q195793|lt=kanjō}} in {{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} 1 ({{ill|717|Q23532|qid=Q23532}}), but *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*<ref name="kamigami">Edited by Ken’ichi Tanigawa, *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Places, Vol. 8 Hokuriku*, Hakusuisha, November 1985.</ref> states that there is no corroborating evidence and that there are various theories regarding its origin, introducing the following views.

# {{ill|Noto Province|cs|Provincie Noto|de|Provinz Noto|es|Provincia de Noto|fa|ولایت نوتو|fr|Province de Noto|gl|Provincia de Noto|id|Provinsi Noto|it|Noto (provincia)|ja|能登国|ko|노토국|lt|Noto žemė|nl|Noto (provincie)|pt|Província de Noto|ru|Ното (провинция)|simple|Noto Province|sk|Noto (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ното|tr|Noto (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ното|zh|能登國|zh_min_nan|Noto-kok|zh_yue|能登國|qid=Q1047671}} separated from {{ill|Echizen Province|Q1047144|qid=Q1047144}} in {{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} 2 ({{ill|718|Q23534|qid=Q23534}}), was merged into Etchū Province in {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 13 ({{ill|741|Q23597|qid=Q23597}}), and then separated again in {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}} 1 ({{ill|AD 757|Q31135|qid=Q31135}}). According to Kitarō Hayashi’s *Fushiki Ichinomiya Keta Shrine*<ref name="tsuite">Tawaratarō Taguchi and Kitarō Hayashi, *Materials on Keta Shrine, Keikō-ji, and the Provincial Temple*, Takaoka, year unknown.</ref>, from Tenpyō 13 (741) to Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757), the {{ill|Keta Taisha|Q11129340|qid=Q11129340}} of {{ill|Hakui District, Ishikawa|Q1130953|qid=Q1130953}} would have been the Ichinomiya of all Etchū, and therefore the transfer of its spirit to this site, which was the location of the provincial capital, likely occurred around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757).
# *History of Takaoka City*<ref name="shishijou">Edited by the Takaoka City History Compilation Committee, *History of Takaoka City, Vol. 1*, Seirin Shoin, September 1959.</ref> suggests that when Noto Province was merged into Etchū Province, the foremost shrine in the province requiring official worship by the {{ill|Kokushi (official)|az|Kokuşi (vəzifə)|de|Kokushi|es|Kokushi|fa|کوکوشی|ff|Kokushi (official)|fr|Kokushi|it|Kokushi (ufficiale)|ja|国司|ko|고쿠시|pt|Kokushi|ru|Кокуси|sr|Кокуши|uk|Кокусі|vi|Kokushi|zh|國司|qid=Q1351234}} was Keta Taisha in Hakui District, but because it was too far from the provincial capital, a distant worship site was established near the capital, which later became an independent shrine after Noto separated.
# *Old Shrine Records of Etchū Province Shikinaisha*<ref>Included in *Shintō Taikei, Shrine Section 34: Etchū, Echigo, and Sado Provinces*, Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, July 1986.</ref> states that after Noto Province separated from Etchū, the shrine was founded by inviting the spirit of Keta Taisha of Noto, and thus was called “New Keta Myōjin.” This name also appears in the later *Hakusan no Ki*<ref name="hakusan">*Hakusan no Ki* is the oldest of the origin texts preserved by Shirayama Hime Shrine and is designated an Important Cultural Property.</ref>.

Other traditions cited by Hayashi claim the shrine was founded by {{ill|Gyōki|Q1136664|qid=Q1136664}} in {{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} 2 (718) during the reign of {{ill|Empress Genshō|Q235343|qid=Q235343}}, but no materials support this, and it is considered an imitation of the founding legend of {{ill|Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|qid=Q11458557}}’s affiliated temple. *Foundational Research on the Ichinomiya System of Medieval Provinces*<ref name="kiso">Edited by the Medieval Ichinomiya System Research Group, Iwata Shoin, February 2000.</ref> also introduces the view that the shrine was founded by inviting a divided spirit from Keta Taisha around Tenpyō-hōji 1 (757).

According to *Hakusan no Ki*<ref name="hakusan" />, when Noto Province separated from Etchū during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}}, the shrine that had been the second-ranking shrine of Etchū became the Ichinomiya, after which a dispute arose between this shrine and {{ill|Imizu Shrine|Q11458557|qid=Q11458557}}, eventually resulting in this shrine becoming the Ichinomiya.

In {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}), the shrine was listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} and became a Shikinaisha. It was granted the divine rank of {{ill|Senior Third Rank|Q11123261|qid=Q11123261}} in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 3 (784) and received official offerings in {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} 8 (908).

Although the shrine is listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} in some manuscripts of the *Engishiki*, other manuscripts list Imizu Shrine instead, leading to scholarly debate.

== From the medieval period onward ==
Various historical records describe incidents, reconstructions, patronage by the {{ill|Maeda clan|Q578033|qid=Q578033}}, destruction during wars, restoration in the early modern period, and the effects of the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}} policy in the Meiji era, which led to the abolition of the affiliated temple Keikō-ji.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 (1873), the shrine was ranked as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}, and in 1907 it was designated a government-offering shrine. On January 19, {{ill|1931|Q18782|qid=Q18782}}, the main hall was designated a former {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|Q1139795|qid=Q1139795}} (later an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622}}).

== Shrine grounds ==
[[File:Keta-jinja (Takaoka), honden.jpg|thumb|Main Hall (National {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622}})]]
The main hall is built in the sangen-sha nagare-zukuri style and preserves characteristics of Muromachi-period shrine architecture.

Other structures include the worship hall, {{ill|Ōtomo Shrine|Q11432351|qid=Q11432351}} dedicated to {{ill|Ōtomo no Yakamochi|Q386308|qid=Q386308}}, and a traditional site of the former Etchū Sōja.

== Major festivals ==
Each year on {{ill|April 18|Q2521|qid=Q2521}}, a spring grand festival is held, featuring the “Nirami Shishi” lion dance, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Takaoka City, and since 2022 the ceremonial procession of the envoy has been revived after about 30 years.

== Cultural properties ==
== Important Cultural Properties (National designation) ==
* Main Hall (structure) – designated January 19, 1931.

== Takaoka City designated cultural properties ==
* Tangible Cultural Property: Wooden guardian lion-dog pair – designated March 27, 1961.
* Intangible Folk Cultural Property: Nirami Shishi of Keta Shrine – designated December 4, 1996.

== Visitor information ==
; Address
* Fushiki Ichinomiya 1-10-1, Takaoka City, Toyama Prefecture

; Access
* Nearest station: {{ill|Etchū-Kokubu Station|Q11636382|qid=Q11636382}} on the {{ill|Himi Line|Q5357535|qid=Q5357535}} (about 15 minutes on foot)
* From Takaoka Station or Shin-Takaoka Station, take a {{ill|Kaetsunou Bus|Q6346040|qid=Q6346040}} and get off at “Fushiki Ichinomiya”
